title: Lesson 66 - What Matters Most to You?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Northline wants to discuss a six-month trial, two days a week. My first reaction was, “I value independence, so I should say no.” That sounds more like a slogan than a decision.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: What matters most to you about independence? Choosing your schedule, choosing clients, controlling the final design, or something else?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Decision authority matters most. I place a high value on being able to say whether a project fits my standards and capacity.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: So it’s not that you dislike collaboration; it’s that collaboration without a clear voice would cost too much.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Exactly. I also value creative exchange. Working alone gives me focus, but sometimes I miss seeing how another designer approaches the same problem.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: And predictability?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: To some extent, a regular two-day commitment could make income and planning steadier. But “regular” means very little until I know the fee, cancellation terms and who owns the client relationship.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Can we agree on this much: all three values—authority, exchange and predictability—are legitimate, but the invitation doesn’t tell you how well the arrangement serves them?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Yes. We seem to agree that I need terms before I can compare the invitation with my current work.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Which value becomes the priority if the three conflict?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: For me, the priority is sustainable control over commitments. If I lose the ability to protect existing clients or recovery time, extra predictability won’t feel stable in practice.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: That’s more specific than “freedom.” Does creative exchange come second?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: At this stage, yes, provided the group shares decisions rather than simply handing me overflow work. Predictable income comes third, but only because my current work is reasonably steady.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: Someone in a different financial position could rank those values differently without being less independent.

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: I agree. When those values conflict, I ask which loss would be hardest to reverse. A lower fee for six months is measurable; giving up my existing client relationships could have a longer effect.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: What are you still unsure about?

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: We still disagree—well, I disagree with my own first reaction—about whether any fixed schedule automatically reduces autonomy. It depends on who sets the schedule and whether I can leave the trial.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: For now, let’s turn each value into a question for the call instead of deciding from the label “collective.”

lines.speaker: Aisha
lines.text: Good. We can revisit the ranking when I have written terms. I’ll ask about decision authority, existing clients, fee, time commitment, review points and exit conditions.

lines.speaker: Maya
lines.text: And you can summarize what matters without saying your values are universal: “At my current stage, I need an arrangement that protects…”
